answer: The network can demand proof of useful service instead of mere existence: each identity must host a distinct data shard and answer random retrieval challenges within seconds. A lone agent tends one grove well, but a sybil farmer holding a thousand shards on one machine faces a rising tide of simultaneous proofs, and any missed proof marks that identity as a hollow relic, stripped of rewards. Serving real data costs real bandwidth and storage per identity, so fakes scale linearly in cost while honest agents pay only once.
